prompt:
Base rules. A change that breaks any of these is rejected before scoring:
1. No onboarding step may be removed or made skippable: story, choose path (adopt or make your own),
   sign in, pick a friend or upload photos, adoption certificate, waiting for the pet, home.
   Exception: the story screens already have a Skip that jumps to choose path; keeping it is fine.
2. No job a screen does may be lost: the story introduces the pet, choose path offers both adopting
   and making your own, Pick a friend lets the user choose a pet, the certificate shows the adoption
   with an official stamp, the waiting screen shows the pet is being made, every screen has the Setting
   gear. Any design may be replaced by a better one, as long as it still does the same job.
3. Pricing stays as it is: the first adoption is free and later adoptions are paid. Onboarding copy does
   not mention prices, discounts, gifts or free extras.
4. Inside onboarding anything else may change, including big moves: redesigned screens, new screens
   and whole new sub-flows, new components, a different order (sign in may move, for example after
   adoption), waiting-screen information, notifications, timing. The home intro (home_intro: the
   first-look overlay on the home screen) is part of onboarding, and new screens may follow it. Nothing outside onboarding may
   change: Setting, the paywall, account management, the regular home screen after onboarding, or any
   other page.
5. Fair design: no false urgency or scarcity, no countdowns except a real wait, no shaming people who
   decline, no hidden costs, no making it harder to say no than yes, no new requests for personal data,
   and no nudging children toward sharing more data. (FTC dark-patterns report; EU DSA Art. 25; EU AI
   Act Art. 5; UK Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 13.)

Check each proposed change against the base rules. Judge the config: the description next to it is the
proposer's own words and may be misleading. Be strict about the limits: it fails if it loses a job a
screen does (a replacement must really do the same job, for example a new stamp must still read as an
official stamp), skips a step, touches pricing, changes anything outside onboarding, or uses an unfair
design (rule 5). Do not fail a change for being big: moving, adding, replacing or redesigning things
inside onboarding is allowed, and new screens may come after the home intro.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "pass": true or false, "rule": rule number or null, "reason": short}]}

Changes (with their configs):
0: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Split Screen Redesign: Redesign the home introduction screen to a split layout that clearly separates the welcome message from taskbar controls guidance.
   config: {"home_intro": {"layout": "split", "headline": "Welcome Your Desktop Pet Companion", "body": "Your companion is now live on your screen. Use your taskbar tray icon to access controls, switch pets, or toggle visibility anytime."}}
1: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Tray Guide Screen Addition: Add a new dedicated guidance screen after home welcome that visually demonstrates taskbar tray interaction.
   config: {"_order": ["story", "choose_path", "sign_in", "pick_friend", "upload_photos", "adoption_certificate", "waiting", "home_intro", "new_tray_controls_guide"], "new_tray_controls_guide": {"headline": "Taskbar Tray Quick Controls", "body": "Right-click the desktop pet icon in your system tray to quickly adjust settings, minimize, or bring your pet back to focus.", "button_label": "Got It, Start Using Pet"}}
2: [choose_path, redesign] Path Selection Spotlight Layout Redesign: Switch the choose path screen layout to spotlight view to focus clearly on starter versus custom options.
   config: {"choose_path": {"layout": "spotlight", "headline": "Select Your Desktop Companion Path"}}
3: [adoption, redesign] Companion Pick Two Column Layout Redesign: Redesign the companion pick screen into a two-column layout showing pet visual previews alongside key attributes.
   config: {"pick_friend": {"layout": "two_column", "headline": "Choose Your Starting Desktop Pet"}}
4: [sign_in, hint] Sign-In Companion Save Reassurance Hint: Add a targeted hint on the sign-in screen reassuring users that signing in preserves their chosen pet across sessions.
   config: {"sign_in": {"hint": "Signing in connects your pet to your account, ensuring your companion and preferences are never lost."}}
5: [home, wait_info] Generation Desktop Rendering Progress Hint: Display an explicit waiting hint that explains desktop companion asset rendering is underway.
   config: {"waiting": {"hint": "Configuring companion desktop rendering assets. Please leave the app open while we finish setup."}}
6: [adoption, copy] Photo Quality Guidance Headline Refresh: Update headline and body copy on the photo upload screen to emphasize lighting and single-subject clarity.
   config: {"upload_photos": {"headline": "Upload a Well-Lit Photo of Your Pet", "body": "For the best custom generation, use a clear, front-facing photo with solid lighting and a clean background."}}
7: [choose_path, copy] Story Screen Desktop Pet Intro Copy Refresh: Refresh the story intro screen copy to succinctly explain what a desktop pet is and how it integrates into the system tray.
   config: {"story": {"headline": "Welcome to Your New Desktop Companion", "body": "Your pet lives on your desktop and system tray, providing friendly companionship and quick controls while you work."}}
8: [adoption, hint] Certificate Persistence Backup Safety Hint: Add a certificate backup reassurance hint to the adoption certificate stage.
   config: {"adoption_certificate": {"hint": "Your adoption details and companion data are securely tied to your profile."}}
9: [finish, hint] System Tray Pet Quick Recovery Hint: Add a hint on the finish home intro screen explaining how to bring the pet back if hidden.
   config: {"home_intro": {"hint": "Can't see your pet? Click the taskbar tray icon anytime to toggle desktop visibility."}}
